summary: Redwood AE+SE walked Sunridge through the model catalog UI, open model selection, benchmark results, and compatibility matrix for Dedicated vs Hosted. Key concerns were latency vs cost tradeoffs, VPC/KMS requirements, and model QA. Agreed to send benchmarks, compatibility matrix, and schedule POC scoping.
transcript:
Header: 2026-12-09 14:00 UTC | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Jamie Lopez (Redwood AE), Priya Sharma (Redwood SE), Mark Ellis (CTO, Sunridge), Sara Kim (ML Engineer), Lena Ortiz (Head of Security)

[00:00] Jamie (AE): Hey everybody, thanks for joining. I'm Jamie from Redwood, and with me is Priya on the SE side. quick agenda: run through the model catalog, show how you pick open models, look at our benchmark results, and then go into compatibility matrix — hardware, quantization, e.g. And then QA and next steps.

[00:18] Mark (Customer): Great, thanks. We're mainly evaluating for clinical notes summarization and triage support. latency is important — under 300ms p50 ideally — but cost is also a hard constraint. we run on GCP today, k8s, some TPU usage for training but inference is mostly on GPUs.

[00:36] Priya (SE): okay thanks, that's helpful. quick qual q: what qps do you expect and what's your average prompt length?

[00:45] Sara (Customer): For pilot probably 30–50 rps, prompt lengths around 600 tokens average, but some longer threads to 2k. also HIPAA-ish data, so we need VPC/on-prem option and KMS integration, audit logs — Lena will follow up on security.

[01:05] Lena (Security): yes SOC 2 plus KMS and SSO, we need customer-managed keys and retention controls. also data residency — some PHI must stay in US-east.

[01:18] Jamie: totally understood. we'll show the private deployment options later — Redwood Private with dedicated VPC and KMS/HSM integration. for now, Priya will start in the model catalog.

[01:30] Priya: jumping in — I'm sharing the model catalog. top left you can filter by task, license, and curated performance profiles. we tag open models e.g., Llama variants, Falcon, Mistral, and community quantized variants. note: some model names in the catalog are normalized — e.g., Llama 2-13b might appear as llama-2-13b-8q for quantized variants.

[02:05] Mark: curious how you surface benchmark data — is that end-to-end or token-only?

[02:12] Priya: good q. we show both: single-request end-to-end latency (including network and runtime overhead for the hosted API) and token throughput for bench runs on dedicated hardware. the UI has a breakdown: tokenizer + model forward + kernel overhead + KV cache hit rate estimates. sometimes the transcription says 'kernel over-head' as 'karnel — overhead', apologies if the export is noisy.

[02:40] Jamie: also worth calling out the Optimize suggestions. if your workload has repeated prefixes, our prefix/KV caching can cut cost a lot. for clinical notes you'll probably see reuse of templates which helps.

[02:55] Sara: on quantization — does Redwood automatically pick quant profiles per model/hardware? we have concerns about quality regressions.

[03:05] Priya: we recommend profiles based on model architecture and sequence length distribution. the compatibility matrix shows supported quantizations for each model and hardware combo — e.g., 8-bit PTQ on A100, 4-bit on H100 for some models, but we flag measured quality deltas. we actually surface a small delta table: rouge/bleu-ish metrics and a human-eval score for chatty tasks. note: those scores are internal evals — please treat as directional.

[03:40] Mark: can you show an example model that meets our latency target with acceptable quality?

[03:46] Priya: yes. i'll pull the benchmark for llama-2-70b distilled vs mistral-70b. Example: on H100 dedicated we see p50 around 220ms for 600 tokens with batching turned off and kv caching warm. quantized 8-bit drops latency ~10% and cost per token by ~30% but we show a small BLEU drop on our summarization prompts.

[04:10] Jamie: (note: some words here transcribed as 'L—meta 70b' in earlier notes) we'll attach the raw bench spreadsheet. the UI also has a compatibility matrix download.

[04:22] Sara: about batching — we worry about tail latency; do you do dynamic batching with latency SLOs?

[04:30] Priya: yes, our serving runtime does continuous batching with per-route latency SLOs. you can configure max batch window or target p95 SLO and it will trade throughput for latency. also automatic fallbacks — if dedicated capacity is saturated we can route to a lower-cost hosted variant, or to a smaller replica. policies are in the routing tab.

[05:00] Lena: from security: what about keys — can we bring our own KMS? and do audit logs show token-level access?

[05:08] Jamie: yes BYOK via customer-managed KMS, and the Private deployment stores audit logs you can ship to your SIEM. per-token anonymized cost traces are available in Console; raw payload logs are optional and can be restricted. we will share SOC 2 artifacts and the KMS integration doc.

[05:30] Mark: ok. pricing — do we pay per-token on hosted and reserved capacity for Dedicated?

[05:36] Jamie: hosted is usage-based per-token and embedding units; Dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly commits and lower unit costs. Optimize suggestions can reduce unit cost by recommending quant profiles and batching configs. we'll send a sample pricing deck.

[05:52] Priya: back to the catalog: notice the compatibility matrix shows columns: model, recommended quant, supported hardware, expected p50/p95 on sample sequence length, and notes about kernel optimizations. for instance certain Llama variants have fused attention kernels on newer runtimes which lowers latency. sometimes the transcript will show 'fused attn' as 'fuse atn' from the ASR.

[06:20] Sara: how do you handle rollouts? we need canary and A/B testing to catch regressions.

[06:26] Priya: Console supports canary rollouts by percent or by header routing, automatic quality regression detection tied to eval suites, and easy rollback. you can pin model versions and test against a baseline. we also integrate with your eval harness if you want continuous evals.

[06:45] Mark: do you have any examples in healthcare?

[06:48] Jamie: yes a few anonymized case studies— we've done summarization pilots with clinics, reduced cost by ~40% via caching+quant, and kept p50 under target. we'll share a redacted case study PDF.

[07:05] Lena: one more: data residency — if we need US-east only, can the Private deployment be restricted?

[07:12] Priya: yes, Dedicated and Private can be region-pinned. Hosted API can be region-targeted but for strict residency Private is recommended. the compatibility matrix will indicate which hardware types are available in which regions.

[07:32] Mark: for the POC, we'd like to run a 2-week benchmark with our prompt set. can Redwood host that?

[07:38] Jamie: absolutely, we can run a bench on Dedicated trial capacity or provide a self-hosted package for Private. typical flow: we replicate your prompt set (Sara to provide), run bench with representative QPS and sequence lengths, produce p50/p95 and cost per 1M tokens, and then recommend a model + quant profile.

[07:56] Sara: about compatibility: we saw mention of kernel selection — do we need to change model code or is that automatic?

[08:02] Priya: automatic. our runtime compiles and picks optimized kernels based on model arch and sequence length distribution. sometimes we recommend small model rewrites or exporting in a specific format for best perf, but mostly it's invisible. the UI will show 'runtime notes' per model.

[08:20] Jamie: quick demo switch — i'll show the bench tab and CSV export. note: some exported model names can be slightly different; e.g., 'mistral-instruct' might export as 'mistral_instr_v1' — we normalize in our compatibility docs.

[08:42] Priya: here's the benchmark CSV: columns include model, hardware, quant, sequence_length, p50_ms, p95_ms, tokens_per_sec, cost_per_1M_tokens_est. you can upload your prompt set and we'll re-run.

[09:05] Mark: any limitations with very long context models? we have long threads to 2k tokens and sometimes pushing to 4k.

[09:12] Priya: runtime supports long context, but kernel selection and KV cache management matter. for 4k we recommend models with optimized attention kernels; compatibility matrix will flag the best options. quantization impact is more pronounced at longer sequences so we show quality vs seq length graphs.

[09:35] Lena: are audit logs immutable? retention policy?

[09:40] Jamie: yes, audit logs are append-only in the Private deployment; retention is configurable and can export to your logging stack. we'll send the audit log spec.

[09:52] (small crosstalk, someone muted/unmuted)

[10:05] Priya: showing the 'recommended model' flow: you can enter workload profile (avg QPS, avg seq length, latency SLO, cost cap) and we'll rank models by expected cost/latency/quality. you can then export a compatibility matrix for your infra.

[10:28] Sara: perfect. about fallbacks — if Dedicated capacity is down or overloaded, is there an automatic route to hosted?

[10:35] Jamie: yep, routing policies support tiered fallbacks: dedicate -> hosted-spot -> hosted standard, or to smaller model variants. all transparent in Console.

[10:50] Mark: any gotchas for HIPAA data while using hosted?

[10:55] Lena: (interjects) we prefer Private for PHI, but if hosted needed, we'd need BAA and strict retention and BYOK.

[11:03] Jamie: agreed. Redwood can sign a BAA for qualifying customers; we'll route you to legal. we'll attach an outline of compliance offerings.

[11:15] Priya: quick demo of Optimize: it will recommend batching window, quant level, and caching options with an estimated cost delta and predicted quality delta. lots of customers use it to get 30–50% unit cost reduction before committing to Dedicated.

[11:38] Mark: ok let's talk timelines — we want a pilot in January.

[11:43] Jamie: sounds good. next steps: Sara to send prompt set and target QPS by 2026-12-10; Jamie will send bench spreadsheet and compatibility matrix by 2026-12-11; Priya to prepare detailed latency/cost estimate by 2026-12-12. we'll schedule a POC scoping call for the week of 2026-12-15.

[11:58] Lena: and send SOC 2 + KMS docs.

[12:05] Jamie: will do. any final q's?

[12:10] Mark: none, that was great. thanks.

[12:15] Jamie: thanks all. Recap and action items in chat.

End of transcript.

Notes: ASR errors present — model names and kernel terms sometimes garbled. Attachments referenced: model-compatibility-matrix.csv (link in follow-up), benchmark-results-raw.xlsx, SOC2-summary.pdf.
questions: Which models in the catalog meet 300ms p50 for 600 tokens?
What are the measured quality deltas for 8-bit vs 4-bit quantization on our summarization prompts?
Can Redwood support a 2-week POC in January with dedicated trial capacity?
